boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named Taylor destinations with documented ways to study, gather, perform, pray, recreate, or view art.

cards.title: LaRita Boren Campus Center
cards.subtitle: “The Stu” campus hub
cards.notes: Use the central seating and services as a practical meet-up point before studying, eating, or connecting with a student-development office.
cards.short_summary: A named campus center combining dining, study space, and student-support offices.
cards.evidence_claim: Taylor describes LaRita Boren Campus Center as a central hub for studying, eating, and connecting with student-development programs.
cards.access_notes: Campus building; consult university event and building-access guidance before visiting.

cards.title: Rediger Chapel & Auditorium
cards.subtitle: Inside LaRita Boren Campus Center
cards.notes: Check the chapel calendar and attend an announced campus chapel, concert, talent show, or other scheduled performance in this auditorium.
cards.short_summary: A 1,641-seat auditorium used for chapel and campus performances.
cards.evidence_claim: Taylor states that Rediger hosts campus chapels, dance competitions, concerts, talent shows, and other events.
cards.access_notes: Event access varies; Taylor lists chapel gatherings on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday at 10 a.m.

cards.title: Zondervan Library Study Spaces
cards.subtitle: Academic building on the Taylor campus map
cards.notes: Choose an individual or group work session, then reserve or use an available study room or study pod according to library procedures.
cards.short_summary: The library provides group and individual study areas, including study rooms and pods.
cards.evidence_claim: Taylor’s student handbook lists group and individual study spaces, 15 group study rooms, and two study pods in Zondervan Library.
cards.access_notes: Handbook lists academic-year hours through midnight Monday–Thursday and Sunday; verify current library access before going.

cards.title: Euler Science Complex Atrium
cards.subtitle: Between Nussbaum and Euler
cards.notes: Bring a project or reading session to the atrium when its flexible seating and open gathering layout suit collaborative work.
cards.short_summary: A large atrium designed for study, music, and events.
cards.evidence_claim: Taylor says the atrium connects Nussbaum and Euler and provides a large gathering area for study, musical performances, and events.
cards.access_notes: Located in an academic complex; building access and event setup may affect availability.

cards.title: Mitchell Theater
cards.subtitle: Rupp Communication Arts Center
cards.notes: Look for a Taylor Theatre production or other posted performance, and use the venue name when checking event details and tickets.
cards.short_summary: A flexible, tiered theater where Taylor Theatre stages most productions.
cards.evidence_claim: Taylor identifies Mitchell Theater as the space where Taylor Theatre practices and performs and says it hosts most theatrical productions.
cards.access_notes: Attend scheduled productions or events; performance access and ticketing vary.

cards.title: Taylor Lake
cards.subtitle: Campus lake and beachfront
cards.notes: Plan a daytime outdoor gathering at the beachfront, pavilion, or volleyball courts, observing posted lake rules and lifeguard coverage.
cards.short_summary: A campus lake with volleyball courts, picnic facilities, and seasonal lifeguards.
cards.evidence_claim: Taylor lists beach volleyball courts, bonfire pits, a pavilion, picnic tables, grills, and certified lifeguards during summer lake hours.
cards.access_notes: Lifeguards are on duty during summer lake hours; confirm seasonal availability and activity rules first.

cards.title: Memorial Prayer Chapel
cards.subtitle: Central campus, between academic and residential buildings
cards.notes: Use the chapel’s main seating, private prayer rooms, or outdoor alcoves for quiet reflection while respecting others using the space.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated prayer chapel with group seating, private rooms, and outdoor alcoves.
cards.evidence_claim: Taylor says the Memorial Prayer Chapel was created specifically for prayer and includes a 75-seat chapel, two private prayer rooms, and outdoor alcoves.
cards.access_notes: Designed for prayer; keep visits quiet and check campus access guidance.

cards.title: Butz-Carruth Recital Hall
cards.subtitle: Attached to Smith-Hermanson Music Center
cards.notes: Watch for scheduled recitals or concerts, then arrive for the listed program rather than treating this performance and class space as drop-in seating.
cards.short_summary: A 218-seat recital hall with concert pianos and performance acoustics.
cards.evidence_claim: Taylor describes Butz-Carruth Recital Hall as a 218-seat venue for stage performances, recordings, classes, and conferences.
cards.access_notes: Use during publicly listed performances or events; otherwise it may be reserved for classes or recordings.

cards.title: The Courtroom in Ayres Hall
cards.subtitle: Ayres Alumni Memorial Hall
cards.notes: Look for a lecture or special event that names The Courtroom, especially an Ethics Bowl-related program, and attend through the event’s instructions.
cards.short_summary: A tiered SMART classroom modeled after government seating.
cards.evidence_claim: Taylor says The Courtroom is in Ayres Hall and is used for lectures and special events, including Ethics Bowl competitions.
cards.access_notes: Primarily a classroom and event venue; access depends on academic and event schedules.

cards.title: Boren Art Gallery
cards.subtitle: Helena Memorial Hall
cards.notes: Visit during the gallery’s published hours to view the permanent collections and current exhibition; use the stated accessible entrance if needed.
cards.short_summary: A campus gallery showing Western, Indiana, and rotating art exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: Taylor states that the Boren Art Gallery houses its Western and Indiana art collections, has rotating exhibitions, and offers free admittance.
cards.access_notes: Taylor publishes academic-year hours: Wednesday noon–5 p.m.; Monday and Friday visits are by appointment.
